title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 14
summary: Oil edged higher as traders weighed a US threat to impose unprecedented economic measures on Iran, with the war that snarled the Strait of Hormuz in its sixth month.

title: Pricey Diesel to Push Harvest Season Costs Higher, Says Tom Kloza
summary: Tom Kloza, chief oil advisor to Gulf Oil, says that disruption in the global oil market from the Iran war is likely to make this harvest season extremely costly as average diesel prices extends over $5 a gallon. Kloza also discussed the impact economic pressure on Iran and said that that likely means the US won't have 'full and unfettered access' to the global oil markets.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Stocks Fall on Signs US Consumer Is Slowing Down: Markets Wrap
summary: Stocks retreated after the economy’s main engine showed signs of cooling, overshadowing optimism around bets the Federal Reserve will stay on hold in September.

title: Winning War With Iran Requires Patience, Says Retired Army Brigadier General
summary: Retired US Army Brigadier General Mark Kimmitt said winning a war with Iran will require patience on the side of the United States because Iran follows a model of resistance and will consider the war a win if they don't lose.  Kimmitt also cast doubt on the idea that the US could win the war with an air campaign alone as the Trump administration moves to put economic rather than military pressure on Iran.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: White Sugar Rally Adds to Already-Steep Refining Margins
summary: White sugar futures in London rose for a third straight week, slightly outpacing raw sugar and keeping refining margins near their highest levels in two years.

title: US Stocks Slip From Highs as Investors Weigh Consumer Demand
summary: US equities slipped from all-time highs as new data showed that consumer spending softened in July.

title: Luigi Mangione Pleads Guilty in US Case Over CEO Killing
summary:
Luigi Mangione pleaded guilty in a federal case over the fatal shooting of UnitedHealth Group executive Brian Thompson in December 2024.

 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Mangione Admits to Killing Healthcare CEO Brian Thompson
summary: Luigi Mangione pleaded guilty to federal stalking charges related to the fatal shooting of UnitedHealth Group Inc. executive Brian Thompson. Mangione admitted on Friday in New York federal court that he shot and killed Thompson on Dec. 4, 2024. He faces life in prison. Mangione's attorney, Karen Friedman Agnifilo, US Attorney for the Southern District Jamie McDonald and NYPD Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch all spoke outside the court.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Gold Has Been in Bull Market for 25 Years, Wilson Says
summary: Mike Wilson, Morgan Stanley chief US equity strategist and CIO, talks about using gold as a defensive asset to protect your portfolio. He says gold has been in a bull market for 25 years. He speaks on "Bloomberg Money." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Braskem Optimistic on Talks With Creditors as Deadline Looms
summary: Braskem SA said negotiations with creditors are advancing as part of an effort to restructure the troubled petrochemicals producer’s finances.

title: Odd Lots: How El Niños Actually Work
summary:
Forecasters are predicting record-breaking intensity for this year's emerging El Niño. But how do El Niños actually work?

On this episode of the Odd Lots podcast, Justin Mankin, professor of geography at Dartmouth, joins Joe Weisenthal and Tracy Alloway to explain this weather phenomenon, using a space heater as an analogy. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Election Angst Fuels Bruising Week in Brazil Markets
summary: Brazilian assets are posting some of the biggest losses in the world this week amid growing angst over the October presidential election.

title: Russian Regions Face New Fuel Crunch as Kyiv Hits Refineries
summary: Several regions of Russia are facing fuel shortages again after Ukraine resumed almost daily attacks on oil refineries in the country.

title: Ankur Crawford on Choosing a Job You Love
summary:
Ankur Crawford, Executive Vice President and Portfolio Manager of the Alger Capital Appreciation, Alger Focus Equity, and Alger Spectra Strategies joins Barry for a conversation about how she builds an investment strategy. They also discuss her journey from engineering to investment, along with understanding AI and compute investment cycles. 

 (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Treasuries Rise as Weak Retail Sales Dampen Fed Rate-Hike Expectations
summary: The US two-year yield extended its decline for a third straight week after soft July retail sales data further eroded expectations for Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes in the coming months.

title: Everybody’s Business: The Rise of AI Music
summary: On this episode of the Everybody's Business podcast, Bloomberg reporter Ashley Carman joins Max Chafkin and Stacey Vanek Smith to unpack the surge of AI-generated music and what streaming platforms like Spotify and Deezer are doing about the backlash from listeners and artists. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Weak Dollar, Fed Outlook Fuel Broad Emerging-Market Rally
summary: Emerging-market stocks and currencies extended the week’s gains on Friday as a shift in the US interest-rate outlook added to bullish sentiment around artificial intelligence.

title: Dollar Touches Lowest Since May as Retail Data Dims Fed Bets
summary: The dollar fell to the lowest since May after an unexpectedly weak report on US retail sales dimmed expectations for an interest-rate hike from the Federal Reserve.

title: The $20 Million Boom in Women's Volleyball
summary: Women’s volleyball is attracting serious investment as League One Volleyball sells team ownership stakes at valuations around $20 million. LOVB Pro Commissioner Sandra Idehen joins Bloomberg Open Interest to explain why the sport’s massive youth participation, growing college audiences and emerging star athletes could help turn professional volleyball into America’s next major women’s sports league. (Source: Bloomberg)
